title: Document and harden the AI claim filer before bridge integration
goal: Capture the redacted evidence from the successful live Allstate filing, document the current Retell/CLI deployment boundary, and resolve the production-safety questions in the claim packet, readiness gates, post-call extraction, and JobNimbus writeback before file:claim is exposed through the Render bridge.
doneCriteria: A redacted operational record explains the successful Allstate filing path, result capture, manual cleanup, and writeback method without client PII or secrets.
The handoff states whether file:claim is local CLI only or exposed anywhere live and identifies the live Retell configuration generation without IDs or secrets.
Retell post-call custom analysis fields are documented and configured in code, or the writeback clearly treats transcript-derived values as unverified proposals.

The company-approved standard answers remain: no injuries reported, home habitable, temporary repairs made, and Titan Reconstruction is the contractor. Current file evidence or Chance's explicit instruction overrides a default when a claim differs.
Missing-policy readiness is carrier-aware and consistent with the Wave playbook instead of universally blocking when alternate lookup is viable.
Post-call JobNimbus proposals keep claim, adjuster, and status values in fields and use one short operational note consistent with Chance's note rules.
Existing-claim confirmation is distinguishable from a newly filed claim in the extracted outcome.
Fixture-safe tests cover a normal filing candidate, an existing-claim duplicate guard, missing/unknown standard answers, and post-call extraction confidence.
constraints: Do not place another live carrier call for this task.
Do not perform a live JobNimbus write, Gmail send, Quo send, deploy, or environment change.
Do not commit client PII, call transcripts, call IDs, phone numbers, credentials, or Retell/Twilio identifiers.
Normal Git is the primary handoff; use the artifact mailbox only if Git fails.
Do not expose file:claim on the production bridge until Codex reviews the result and Chance approves deployment.

log.note: Created after code review and fixture dry runs. The architecture is strong and a real Allstate filing reportedly succeeded; production questions were posted to PR #1 in comment 4936725671.

Chance confirmed the four standard filing answers are intentional business defaults: no injuries, habitable home, temporary repairs made, and Titan Reconstruction as contractor. Preserve them unless current evidence or Chance identifies an exception.

Answered all 7 review questions in the PR thread and landed the fixture-safe hardening. Q3: post-call analysis schema is now configured in code (postCallAnalysisSchema in retell.js), field names matched to postCallWriteback; transcript-derived values stay flagged transcript-guess. Q5: policy readiness is carrier-aware (warning by default, hard-block only when carrier.requiresPolicyNumber). Q6: writeback keeps claim/adjuster/status in FIELDS + one short operational note. Q7: outcome distinguishes existing_claim_confirmed (status_follow_up goal) from claim_filed. Q4: the four business defaults were PRESERVED per Chance. Redacted operational record added at docs/operational-record-claim-filing.md; deployment truth documented (file:claim is local CLI only, not on the bridge). Fixture-safe tests added to selftest.js. No live call/write/deploy.

result.summary: Claim filer hardened for production review: post-call schema in code, carrier-aware policy readiness, writeback field/note hygiene, existing-vs-new outcome, redacted operational record. Business defaults preserved.
result.verification: npm run check exit 0; 16 new fixture-safe checks (extraction, outcome distinction, note hygiene, no-result, spelled-out claim parse, note-ownership guard). No live actions.
